questions.stem: A Namar Mattresses, a family-owned firm manager argues, "We should add a standard 30 percent to whatever it costs us to make." Which pricing method is being described?
questions.explanation: Cost-plus pricing sets the price by adding a fixed percentage or amount to unit cost. It is simple but ignores demand and competitors, so it can leave money on the table or price a product out of the market. Value-based pricing would start from what buyers are willing to pay instead of from cost.
questions.hint: A fixed percentage added to cost is the defining feature.

options.misconception: mistakes a markup rule for grouping products
confuses a cost markup with a high initial price
assumes the markup reflects customer willingness to pay

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Inverness Stationery, a small firm sells two Stonebridge items separately for $60 and $54. A bundle priced 22 percent below the sum of the separate prices would cost how much?
questions.explanation: The separate prices add to $114. A 22 percent discount removes $25, leaving a bundle price of $89. Adding without discounting ignores the promotion, quoting the discount reports the saving rather than the price, and applying the discount twice would overstate the reduction. Bundling works when buyers value the combination.
questions.hint: Add the two prices, then subtract the stated percentage of that sum.

options.misconception: adds the separate prices without applying the discount
reports only the discount amount, not the final price
applies the discount twice

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Graystone Cameras, a small firm wants to sell a technical product in Yewton that needs demonstration and expert advice before purchase. Which channel is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Products that require education and demonstration are best sold through channels with knowledgeable salespeople, such as a direct sales force or specialised dealers. High-touch channels let the seller explain features and answer questions, which reduces buyer uncertainty. Self-service or vending channels work for simple, frequently bought items, not complex ones.
questions.hint: Match the channel's ability to explain to the product's complexity.
questions.learningObjective: match channel design to product characteristics

options.text: Any channel, since channels do not affect technical sales
options.misconception: denies that channel choice depends on product complexity
mistakes a low-touch channel for one needing expertise

options.text: A direct sales force or specialised dealers that can explain the product
Mass self-service retail with no staff
options.misconception: ignores the need for explanation and advice

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Umbra Outdoor Gear, a national firm decides to stock its product in only one carefully chosen retailer per city in Harborview to maintain a premium image and tight control. Which distribution intensity is this?
questions.explanation: Exclusive distribution means granting very few outlets the right to sell a product in a given area, which supports a premium image and close control over service and presentation. Selective distribution uses a limited but greater number of outlets, while intensive distribution aims for as many outlets as possible. One retailer per city is the hallmark of exclusivity.
questions.hint: One outlet per area points to the most restrictive intensity.

options.misconception: assumes many outlets rather than one per area
confuses a single outlet with several chosen outlets
mistakes tight control with maximum coverage
